all_quick_tuner_timings.justification: The best p99 so far came from iter 6 (66.27 ms) with C1, very low scheduling granularity (200k), and moderate busy-poll (200). Iter 9 pushed latency_ns even lower (2 M) and busy-poll to 400, but the gain was lost and latency rose to 69.13 ms. This suggests we may have overshot the sweet spot on busy-poll. To keep exploring while staying in the proven low-latency region, I slightly relax granularity (150k vs 200k), nudge latency_ns back up to 2.5 M, and dial back busy-poll to 300. The combination should stress-test the boundary between iter 6 and iter 9 without risking a major regression and still leave room for further refinement in later iterations.

all_quick_tuner_timings.justification: The best known point (latency_p99 = 66.27) used C1 and 200 ns busy-poll with 3 ms latency_ns.  To keep exploring in budget, I slightly reduce latency and busy-poll (cheaper wake-ups, less network interrupt latency) while nudging min_granularity up (less pre-emption overhead) and tightening migration_cost_ns (faster task placement).  These are safe changes that stay close to the incumbent region yet probe a new combination.

Splitting the difference—slightly higher granularity (300k), slightly lower busy-poll (180), tighter migration_cost (80k)—should probe the sweet-spot while staying in the safe region already sampled, yet introduce enough variation to keep exploring rather than locking in.
